title: KV micrograph mapper for staggered tensor/pipeline sharding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: When running mixed tensor- and pipeline-parallel topologies with continuous batching, the KV cache allocation pattern becomes fragmented across GPUs leading to memory hotspots, increased cross-GPU communication, and backend stalls during prefetch/spill operations. Goal: design and implement a KV mapping layer (Micrograph Mapper) that produces stable, low-latency shard assignments for KV entries across staggered tensor/pipeline layouts while enabling lightweight local replication for hot prefixes and efficient spill-to-CPU paths for cold data. This ticket covers design, prototype, and initial rollout gating on perf and correctness.
technical_summary: Introduce a runtime Micrograph Mapper that: (1) computes deterministic placement keys using token-prefix affinity and pipeline stage ownership; (2) supports two placement modes — anchored (stable per-prefix placement) and elastic (load-aware remap with bounded churn); (3) exposes per-GPU memory budgets and a prioritized eviction/refill policy with CPU spill and async prefetch; (4) provides a small replicated hotset (N-way) for top-k prefixes to avoid synchronous cross-GPU KV fetches; (5) integrates with the scheduler to favor local KV hits during continuous batching and long context sequences.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No correctness regressions on unit and e2e tests (identical logits for pinned model variants). 2) End-to-end p95 latency improves or remains within +3% for TPxPP mixed topologies under representative loads. 3) Peak GPU KV memory fragmentation reduced by >=20% on large-sequence workloads in our stress harness. 4) CPU spill path saturates only under >80% memory pressure and recovers gracefully. 5) Feature gated and rolloutable via runtime flag and console toggle.
test_plan: - Unit tests for deterministic mapping functions and remap bounds. - Integration tests with mixed tensor/pipeline topologies (TP=2, PP=4, TP=4/PP=2) across multi-node CI. - Stress tests: long-context (64k tokens) live replay on replay-cluster. - Fault injection: GPU eviction/slow NVLink sim to verify async prefetch. - Nightly perf job comparing baseline runtime-1.25 vs candidate branch.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off by default on hosted; internal dogfood on Dedicated. 2) Stage 1: small-scale internal cluster (2 customers, low QPS) with aggressive telemetry. 3) Stage 2: enable for low-latency routes and monitor p95/p99 and KV miss metrics. 4) Full rollout if metrics stable for 72 hours; rollback via runtime flag.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: Remapping churn causing transient latency spikes. Mitigation: bound remap rate and prefer anchored mode; provide explicit canary. - Risk: Hotset replication increases GPU memory. Mitigation: adaptive hotset sizing based on live hit-rate telemetry. - Risk: CPU spill becomes a throughput choke. Mitigation: async staged spill with prefetch backpressure and configurable spill concurrency.
perf_results: Spike (2026-02-28): prototype reduced tail NVLink fetch count by 37% on TP2xPP4 synthetic workload
Microbench (2026-03-02): 14% p50 improvement and 9% p95 improvement on long-context synthesis with anchored mode enabled (16-GPU testbed)
Memory compaction test (2026-03-04): fragmentation metric (free-run variance) down from 0.42 to 0.28 on average across traces
implementation_notes: - Mapper lives in kv-router module and exposes a compact placement table serialized in runtime state for fast rehydration. - Placement table updates are coordinated per-pipeline-epoch to avoid mid-request remaps. - Use jemalloc stats and per-GPU ring allocator metrics for fragmentation signals. - Prefetch uses dedicated I/O worker pool with per-gpu credit system to avoid cross-stream contention.

2026-03-03: Debugged eviction race — root cause: prefetch worker re-entrant schedule on same ring leading to double-free candidate. Patch proposed in kv-utils PR 129.
2026-03-05: Perf run with patch applied — fragmentation improved and p95 stable. Preparing canary config and console toggle for dogfood cluster.
2026-03-06: In-progress: wiring rollout flags to console, adding telemetry dashboards (KV local hit-rate, remap-events/sec, spill-latency). Assigned QA for canary validation.
